Attach pre-landmark covariates to a landmark dataset

Source: R/add_landmark_covariates.R
add_landmark_covariates.Rd

add_landmark_covariates() adds one column per selected longitudinal variable to a landmark_tbl. For every subject-landmark row, the value is derived only from that subject's measurements taken at or before the landmark, so no information from after the landmark leaks into the covariates. Each variable is derived in one of two ways:

  • locf: last observation carried forward, optionally limited to a lookback window.

  • lme: the subject-specific value at the landmark predicted from a linear mixed-effects model fitted separately for every variable and landmark.

Rows are never added or removed, and .time/.status are untouched. Subjects with no usable measurement keep their row with a missing value.

Usage

add_landmark_covariates(
  landmark_data,
  longitudinal_data,
  id,
  time,
  locf = NULL,
  lme = NULL,
  include_at_landmark = TRUE,
  lookback = NULL,
  lme_args = list(),
  names = NULL,
  progress = getOption("tidylandmark.progress", interactive())
)

Arguments

landmark_data

A landmark_tbl, as returned by landmark_data() (or by a previous call to add_landmark_covariates()).

longitudinal_data

A data frame with one row per measurement occasion (multiple rows per subject). Rows whose id does not appear in landmark_data are ignored, and their number is reported in a message.

id

<tidy-select> The subject identifier column in longitudinal_data. It must be non-missing and have the same type as the id used in landmark_data(); types are never coerced implicitly.

time

<tidy-select> Numeric, finite, non-missing measurement time. It must be on the same time scale and origin as the time given to landmark_data(); this cannot be checked automatically. Measurements before time zero (e.g. screening visits) are allowed.

locf, lme

<tidy-select> Columns of longitudinal_data to derive by last observation carried forward and by linear mixed-effects model, e.g. locf = c(treatment, stage) and lme = c(bili, albumin). Either may be NULL (the default), but not both. Rename inside the selection to name a derived column, e.g. lme = c(bili_lme = bili). lme variables must be continuous numeric.

include_at_landmark

If TRUE (default), a measurement taken exactly at the landmark (\(t = s\)) may be used. If FALSE, only measurements strictly before the landmark (\(t < s\)) are used. Applies to both methods.

lookback

locf only. NULL (default) carries values forward without a limit. A single non-negative number only uses measurements within that window: \(s - t \le\) lookback. Older values give NA.

lme_args

lme only. A named list of model options:

  • random_slope: FALSE (default) fits a random intercept; TRUE adds a random slope for time.

  • adjust: NULL (default) or a one-sided formula of fixed-effect adjustment terms, e.g. ~ age + sex. Variables come from landmark_data, so they are baseline values (or covariates added by an earlier call). Use .t for the time since the landmark, e.g. ~ sex * .t for sex-specific slopes.

  • REML: passed to lme4::lmer(). Default TRUE.

  • control: an lme4::lmerControl() object. Default lme4::lmerControl().

  • min_subjects: the fewest subjects with measurements needed to fit a model (default 5). With random_slope = TRUE, this many subjects must have at least two measurements.

names

NULL (default) or a template for derived column names, in which "{.col}" is replaced by the source variable and "{.method}" by "locf" or "lme", e.g. "{.col}_{.method}". Columns renamed in the selection keep their new name. A derived name that already exists in landmark_data is an error; existing columns are never overwritten.

progress

Show a progress bar while fitting mixed models? Defaults to the tidylandmark.progress option, or interactive() if it is unset.

Value

landmark_data with one new column per selected variable (locf columns first, then lme), appended after the existing columns. The class and configuration are kept, and the configuration records how each derived column was made: method, source variable, options, the LOCF audit trail, and for LME the fitted models and their diagnostics. The printed header lists the derived columns and their method.

Details

LOCF

For landmark \(s\), subject \(i\) and variable \(v\), the value is the last non-missing measurement of \(v\) at time \(t \le s\) (or \(t < s\) when include_at_landmark = FALSE), provided it is within lookback. Each variable is handled separately, so a visit where one variable is missing still contributes the others. Selection depends only on id and time, never on row order. Any column type works, and the type (including factor levels) is preserved. The time since each carried-forward measurement is stored in the metadata for auditing.

If a subject has two different non-missing values of an locf variable at the same time, the function errors and lists the affected subjects and times rather than choosing one arbitrarily. Exact duplicates are collapsed.

LME

For every lme variable \(v\) and landmark \(s\), an independent Gaussian model is fitted with lme4::lmer() to the non-missing measurements, taken at or before \(s\), of the subjects in the risk set at \(s\):

$$Y_{ij} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 (t_{ij} - s) + \gamma^\top x_i + b_{0i} [+ b_{1i}(t_{ij} - s)] + \epsilon_{ij}$$

where \(x_i\) are the optional adjust terms. Time is centred at the landmark and rescaled internally for numerical stability, which does not change the predictions. The derived value is the conditional prediction at \(t = s\) including the subject's random effects (predict(fit, re.form = NULL)), i.e. \(\hat\beta_0 + \hat\gamma^\top x_i + \hat b_{0i}\). A subject with a single measurement is kept; their prediction is shrunk towards the population trajectory. A subject with no measurement before the landmark, or with missing adjust values, gets NA rather than a population-only prediction. Different values recorded at the same time are treated as replicate measurements.

Each fit gets a status: "ok"; "warning" when lme4::lmer() warned (e.g. about convergence) or the fit is singular (lme4::isSingular()); or "failed" when there were too few subjects or lme4::lmer() gave an error. Failed fits give NA for that variable at that landmark without affecting other fits, and a warning lists every fit that was not "ok". There is no automatic fallback from a random slope to a random intercept.

Standard errors in a second-stage survival model treat LME-derived values as known, so they understate uncertainty.

See also

landmark_data() to build the risk sets first.

Examples

subjects <- data.frame(
  patient_id    = 1:10,
  followup_days = c(20, 30, 48, 65, 85, 110, 145, 190, 250, 270),
  event         = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 1, 0, 1)
)
visits <- data.frame(
  patient_id = c(6L, 6L, 6L, 7L, 7L, 7L, 10L, 10L),
  visit_day  = c(0, 45, 90, 0, 50, 120, 60, 140),
  treatment  = c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1),
  biomarker  = c(25, 20, 17, 23, NA, 18, 24, 20)
)

lm_dat <- subjects |>
  landmark_data(
    patient_id, followup_days, event,
    landmarks = c(30, 60, 90), horizon = 180
  ) |>
  add_landmark_covariates(
    visits, id = patient_id, time = visit_day,
    locf = c(treatment, biomarker)
  )
lm_dat

# Only carry values forward for up to 30 days, under new names
landmark_data(subjects, patient_id, followup_days, event, landmarks = 60) |>
  add_landmark_covariates(
    visits, patient_id, visit_day,
    locf = biomarker, lookback = 30, names = "{.col}_recent"
  )

# Mixed models with the PBC data: log bilirubin by LME, adjusted
# for age, alongside LOCF for albumin
visits_pbc <- transform(pbcseq_visits, log_bili = log(bili))
pbc_lm <- pbcseq_baseline |>
  landmark_data(id, futime, status, landmarks = c(365, 730), horizon = 1825) |>
  add_landmark_covariates(
    visits_pbc, id, day,
    locf = albumin,
    lme = log_bili,
    lme_args = list(adjust = ~ age)
  )
